In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematic analysis of the conformal symmetry breaking in the QCD Lagrangian.
the study of the conformal properties of the local operators in Quantum Chromo Dynamics (QCD) in the leading and the next-to-leading orders of perturbation theory.
the study of the conformal invariances in QCD and its consequences for the anomalous dimensions of the twist-2 operators and evolution of the exclusive and non-forward distribution amplitudes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our results for the anomalous dimension matrices and the corresponding evolution equations are the first ones in the literature to be based on conformal symmetry and the conformal partial-wave expansion.

the conformal symmetry is not an exact symmetry in Quantum Chromodynamics, and the conformal symmetry breaking in the theory is a nontrivial phenomenon, which is not just the consequence of the spontaneous symmetry breaking of the scale invariance.

we have found the next-to-leading-order conformal invariances of the exclusive distribution amplitude and non-forward partons distributions in the flavour singlett channel in the next-to-next-to-leading order approximation of the coupling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the conformal consistency relations allow us to obtain the off-diagonal parts in the evolution kernels in the next-to-next-to-leading order of perturbative QCD without any additional calculations in terms of the known one-loop anomalous dimensions of the twist-2 operators and the two-loop anomalous dimensions for the chiral odd sector.

we have derived the anomalous dimensions of the twist-2 operators, the off-diagonal parts for the evolution of exclusive and non-forward distribution amplitudes as well as the off-diagonal evolution kernels for the chiral even parity-odd sector.
the conformal consistency relations are very helpful in the calculation of the anomalous dimensions and evolution kernels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conformal symmetry breaking is the key ingredient of the QCD dynamics and the conformal symmetry is the main tool for the study of the QCD evolution.
the conformal symmetry of the QCD Lagrangian is not an exact symmetry at the quantum level.

the conformal symmetry of Quantum Chromodynamics is broken by the quantum anomalies of the local twist operators, and this breaking leads to the nontrivial spectrum of anomalous dimension matrices in QCD.
